I am 73 years old, and I have farmed my 5 mu of land in Quzhou County for over fifty years. I only finished primary school, but I know this soil better than any book. This year, just like every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same 5 mu — that is the only system that works on the North China Plain. I plant wheat in October, harvest it in early June, and immediately plant maize in the same field. I stopped growing cotton a few years ago because my back cannot handle the bending for picking anymore, and my son works in the county town so he cannot help.

For wheat, I will use improved seed — Luyuan 502, which I have used for several years and it does well here. Before planting, I run the rotary tiller over the field to break up the soil. I put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose, then topdress with urea when the wheat greens up and again at jointing. I will irrigate four times: before winter to help the wheat survive the cold, and then in spring at green-up, jointing, and heading. I spray herbicide once and fungicide plus insecticide twice. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed Denghai 605 from the agricultural supply shop. Right after I cut the wheat in June, I plant the maize directly into the wheat stubble without tilling — no-tillage saves time, diesel, and labor, and everyone in the village does it now. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea at the big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come. I spray herbicide once and insecticide for corn borer twice. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

I do not calculate fertilizer exactly by the kilo — I buy bags by experience. But roughly, I use about 18 kg nitrogen per mu for wheat and 16 kg for maize, with phosphorus and potassium from the compound bags. I follow what my neighbors do and what the seed shop recommends. I do not try new crops or fancy methods at my age; I stick to what I know works.
